subject: Consolidation economics + runtime fallback checklist
messages:
From: Evan Cruz <evan.cruz@clearmap.io>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@clearmap.io
Date: Tue, 3 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-up: consolidation economics + runtime questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're collecting vendor comparisons for a possible consolidation of our inference stack and I wanted to share the RFP and a few clarifying questions up front. Attached: ClearMap_RFP_v1.pdf.

High-level asks:
- Can you provide a side-by-side cost worksheet (tokens/embeds + infra uplift) vs our incumbent for a 12-month ramp? (we've attached current usage)
- Are there deposit/commitment models + pilot credits? We want to understand how you protect against early migration churn.
- Critically: what compatibility and fallback behavior do you offer if our primary model variant or region hits capacity? We need a short checklist we can put in the SOW.

Our timeline: pilot in July, decision mid-August.

Appreciate a quick initial workbook and a short note on runtime fallbacks.

Best,
Evan
Evan Cruz
Head of Platform Procurement
ClearMap
[Attachment: ClearMap_RFP_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cruz <evan.cruz@clearmap.io>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, procurement@clearmap.io
Date: Tue, 3 Jun 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: consolidation economics + runtime questions

Thanks Evan — saw this first thing. I've attached an initial workbook and an outline of protections we typically propose.

Attachments: Redwood_Initial_Price_v1.xlsx, Redwood_Runtime_Fallbacks_v1.pdf

Summary (very high level):
- 12-month blended estimate (tokens + infra uplift): $0.022/token effective for generation workloads at your projected 18M tokens/month.
- Pilot incentives: 3-month pilot with a $40k pilot credit and waived integration engineering hours for first 30 days.
- Commitment options: monthly consumption, 6/12/24-month reserved pools (we include step-down credits if you commit and then scale slower than expected).
- Fallbacks we recommend for the SOW (short checklist):
  1) Model variant fallback: automatic route to a compatible, lower-cost quantized variant with identical API surface.
  2) Region failover: traffic policy to route to a secondary region within the same cloud provider (data residency permitting).
  3) Graceful degradation: token rate-limits and progressive response shortening to maintain availability.
  4) Canary and rollback: staged rollout for new model versions with automatic rollback on latency/accuracy regressions.

Next steps: want to schedule a 30-min call later today or tomorrow to walk the workbook and confirm a pilot SOW? I can loop in Kimberly to confirm commercial levers.

Thanks,
Jonas
VP, Revenue Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Initial_Price_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, rachel.kim@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Jun 2025 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: RFP follow-up: consolidation economics + runtime questions — negotiation plan

Kimberly / Rachel / Connor — looping you in. ClearMap wants a side-by-side TCO and a short SOW checklist for fallbacks. Below my proposed negotiation posture and asks for discounts/packaging:

Proposed commercial posture (aiming for win + protect margin):
- Offer: 12-month blended token price of $0.022 with a 3-month pilot ($40k credit).
- Concession if they push: early-year credit (20% of first-year consumption up to $60k) in exchange for a 12-month reservation commit at 70% of projected run-rate.
- Technical add-ons: include 20 hours free integration support + one runtime compatibility test (3-day dedicated window).

Packaging notes (options to present):
A) Pure consumption + pilot credit (fastest procurement).
B) 6mo reservation + lower effective unit price (requires procurement sign-off).
C) 12mo reservation + onboarding credits + SLA uplift (dedicated pool option).

Legal/commercial asks:
- Can Legal draft a one-page addendum capturing the fallback checklist + pilot terms (no long contract initially, we use DocuSign for the pilot SOW)?
- Finance: confirm whether we can push the $60k cap on concession and still honor partner-level rebates.

Action items:
- Kimberly: lead the concession approval thread and decide whether we can go to 20% first-year credit.
- Rachel: prepare the short runtime-fallback checklist for SOW; call out model-variant names and quantization expectations.
- Connor: validate the technical 3-day compatibility window and what telemetry we need to collect.

I plan to follow up with Evan with the workbook + one-pager once you confirm.

Thanks,
Jonas

From: Evan Cruz <evan.cruz@clearmap.io>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@clearmap.io
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: consolidation economics + runtime questions

Jonas — appreciate the fast turnaround and the workbook. A few quick clarifications from procurement and infra: 

- Pilot: we can do the 3-month pilot. To de-risk, procurement is asking for a 20% credit on first-year consumption up to $50k (we can stretch to $60k if there are stronger SLA remedies).
- Runtime compatibility: infra wants a signed 3-day dedicated compatibility test window (test plan, metrics, and roll criteria). Can you commit to providing a pass/fail report and the test instrumentation?
- Legal: we'd prefer the pilot SOW as a one-page DocuSign addendum referencing the RFP and the fallback checklist.

If you can confirm the 20% first-year credit (cap at $60k) and provide the signed compatibility test plan, procurement says we can move to a pilot DocuSign by next Monday and start the pilot in mid-July.

Small ask: could you include an export of the workbook that maps their current per-token effective spend -> Redwood effective spend line-by-line? That will help our CFO sign off.

Thanks,
Evan
Head of Platform Procurement
ClearMap
